glycyrrhizic acid, an active component from licorice roots (Glycyrrhiza glabra L.) reduces the severity of the immunosuppression associated with thermal injury and the susceptibility to fungal infection in thermally wounded mice.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of burn‐associated T cells in the susceptibility of thermall injured mice to fungal infection.
the development of new immunomodulators to prevent burn‐associated immunosuppression and the susceptibility of thermically injured mice to C.albicans infection.
the effects of GR on the immune response of thermally injured animals and the role of type 2 T lymphocytes in the susceptibility of thermically injured mice to C.albicans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GR, by inhibiting the type 2 cytokine production by burn‐associated T cells, improves resistance to C. albican infection in thermally burned mice.
GR‐treated CD4+ T‐cells, which are capable of inhibiting type‐2 T cells, can reverse the increased susceptibility of thermally‐injured mice to Candida albicans.

GR‐treated CD4+ T‐cells, which suppress the burn‐associated type‐2 T‐cells, improve the resistance of thermically injured mice to C.albicans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti‐type 1 T cell action of CD4+ cells from GR‐ treated mice was not the main mechanism by which GR reduced the susceptibility of mice to C. albicans.
GR is an effective agent for preventing burn‐associated type II T cell‐induced susceptibility to C. albican infection.
GR can be used to treat burn patients with fungal infection by reducing the susceptibility to fungal infection.
